hypothesis: A fixed 0.5 shrink of the system's industry-neutral scoring transform may reduce industry-linked concentration while preserving more of the default A-leg score ordering than full shrink=1.0. This is a single exploratory contrast against R266; prior R98 industry-neutralization results and this strategy's extensive history are known, so neither discovery nor validation is an untouched holdout.

execution.only_changed_parameter: system neutralize override: industry_l1 with shrink=0.5
execution.implementation: StrategyBacktestService -> BacktestEngine -> existing scoring.neutralize_scoring_columns; candidate transforms are calculated inside each date's HS300 candidate universe.
execution.control: R266 finalized curve/trade caches; byte hashes checked before comparison

known_limitations: R98 previously tested full industry neutralization and industry plus size neutralization; those older results used pre-R125 holder data and 2x costs. R271 is an exploratory updated-score test, not a fresh confirmatory experiment.
R270's initial results had already been exposed before its final byte-identical recalculation; that audit does not restore independence.
R271 reuses a strategy and validation interval examined across many prior rounds; validation is not an untouched holdout.
Industry classification is a current snapshot, not point-in-time historical industry membership.
Score neutralization is not portfolio-level industry neutrality and does not enforce industry quotas.
Macro factor source data may be revised; historical HS300 membership is used.
Only 290 R266 baseline trades are available; concentration and tail estimates have sampling uncertainty.
Panel reload and passing historical backtest do not authorize paper or production deployment.
